narrator.instruct: Fast, gripping, high-energy history storyteller. Excited and urgent, amazed, punchy emphasis on the shocking moments, brisk pace, no long pauses.

miller.instruct: A puzzled, worried old miller in his doorway, half whispering, stunned by the silence.

voice.instruct: Dramatic, amazed opening hook, urgent, hitting 'silent' hard and then dropping to a hush.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One March night in eighteen forty-eight, people near the falls woke up to total silence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No roar. No mist. Just bare wet rock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Strong winds had pushed huge sheets of ice across Lake Erie.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ice plugged the river like a cork in a bottle. And the water just stopped.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For about thirty hours, people walked across the empty riverbed. Some even rode horses!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Others found rusty old muskets lying on the rocks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the ice broke. A giant wall of water came rushing back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Imagine standing right there when Niagara came roaring back to life.
